page: Microsoft Azure E16ps_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the EPSv5 server family. It is powered by an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor with 16 dedicated physical cores operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The architecture is arm64, utilizing the ARMv8 instruction set. The server features 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most compute and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is 1822.6, while the multi-core score reaches 28894.58. Memory bandwidth is measured at 1127.15 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, and 127.65 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-threaded tasks show some limitations, with a weak Geekbench single-core score of 1116.0 and a weak single-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 8.81 GB/sec.

Given its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server is classified as memory-optimized, offering high resource density for memory-intensive applications without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPU hardware. It is appropriate for database operations, as evidenced by a Passmark database score of 10911.19 and Redis SET performance of 22.74 million operations per second. Other fitting workloads include static web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing.
description: The Microsoft Azure E16ps_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine from the EPSv5 family, featuring 16 dedicated physical cores on an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. This server does not include local storage or GPUs but supports Premium Storage. Performance benchmarks place the instance in the average tier for multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and database operations, though single-threaded performance is relatively weak. With its high memory density and dedicated ARM cores, the E16ps_v5 is configured for memory-intensive workloads, database management, static web serving, and multi-threaded applications where local disk storage is not required.
